earth_surface_nT.source: IGRF-14 (ppigrf 2.1.0, IGRF14.shc); coordinates: NASA Open Data Portal, 'NASA Facilities' dataset, https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/nasa-facilities, file https://data.nasa.gov/docs/legacy/NASA_Facilities/NASA_Facilities_rows.csv (sha256 dc10864a161c48d49f71f028ce1ae6b1fcf888ac1f8307c82400444e792cf4cf, accessed 2026-11-15)
earth_surface_nT.note: formula: |B| = sqrt(Be^2 + Bn^2 + Bu^2) from the IGRF model at geodetic lat, lon, height and date; inputs: earth_flight.jsc.coords, date 2026-11-15T19:53:29Z; the source gives no elevation, so the model is evaluated at height 0 km on the WGS84 ellipsoid; here IGRF |B| changes by -23.1 nT per km of height

opm_dynamic_range_nT.source: QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 product page, https://quspin.com/products-qzfm/
opm_dynamic_range_nT.note: QZFM dynamic range ±5 nT (specs.opm.dynamic_range). QuSpin also states the field at the sensor must be reduced to about 50 nT or below; built-in coils cancel residual fields up to 50 nT.

nv_gyromagnetic_ratio_MHz_per_mT.source: SpinDrift calculation; 28.025 MHz/mT is the electron gyromagnetic ratio gamma_e/2pi (CODATA 2022, 28 024.951 3861 MHz/T, rounded to five digits; data/quantum_constants.json electron.gyromagnetic_ratio_over_2pi)

formulas.lunar_upper_bound: |B| <= |B_crustal| + |B_ambient| (upper bound from the triangle inequality; the crustal vector is body-fixed and the ambient vector is GSE, so the two are not added as vectors)

sub_places.notes: Reiner Gamma swirl in Oceanus Procellarum, a strong crustal magnetic anomaly; Tsunakawa et al. (2015) find the near-surface field structure there correlated with the high-albedo markings. The value is the model field at the feature's centre, not the peak of the anomaly. The Moon has no global magnetic field; B_total_nT is an upper bound: the crustal field of a published model (components.crustal_nT) plus the ambient field (components.ambient_nT, the most recent THEMIS-C (ARTEMIS P2) lunar-orbit magnetometer sample (recorded)), because the two vectors are in different frames. B_vector_nT is the crustal part only. Cross-check with a second published model, the spherical-harmonic expansion (degree 449) of the Tsunakawa et al. (2015) surface map by Wieczorek (2018), doi:10.5281/zenodo.3873648 (CC BY 4.0), evaluated here at radius 1737.4 km: 97.8 nT. Published range of lunar surface fields: the Tsunakawa et al. (2015) surface map reaches 718 nT (Crisium antipodal region); the Apollo surface magnetometers measured 3.4 to 327 nT (Dyal, Parkin & Daily 1973). During most of its orbit the Moon is directly exposed to the solar wind, but for 5-6 days every orbit it crosses the tail of Earth's magnetosphere (Dandouras et al. 2023); NOAA describes the tail as stretching well beyond the Moon's orbit at 60 Earth radii. Inside the tail an L1 solar-wind value does not apply.

sub_places.notes: Aitken crater, the northern end of the South Pole-Aitken basin (the basin spans the territory from Aitken crater to the south pole: NASA Science, 'What is the South Pole-Aitken Basin?', https://science.nasa.gov/moon/lunar-craters/what-is-the-south-pole-aitken-basin/ (accessed 2026-11-15)). Tsunakawa et al. (2015) list a well-isolated central magnetic anomaly at Aitken crater. The value is the model field at the crater's centre. The Moon has no global magnetic field; B_total_nT is an upper bound: the crustal field of a published model (components.crustal_nT) plus the ambient field (components.ambient_nT, the most recent THEMIS-C (ARTEMIS P2) lunar-orbit magnetometer sample (recorded)), because the two vectors are in different frames. B_vector_nT is the crustal part only. Cross-check with a second published model, the spherical-harmonic expansion (degree 449) of the Tsunakawa et al. (2015) surface map by Wieczorek (2018), doi:10.5281/zenodo.3873648 (CC BY 4.0), evaluated here at radius 1737.4 km: 31.6 nT. Published range of lunar surface fields: the Tsunakawa et al. (2015) surface map reaches 718 nT (Crisium antipodal region); the Apollo surface magnetometers measured 3.4 to 327 nT (Dyal, Parkin & Daily 1973). During most of its orbit the Moon is directly exposed to the solar wind, but for 5-6 days every orbit it crosses the tail of Earth's magnetosphere (Dandouras et al. 2023); NOAA describes the tail as stretching well beyond the Moon's orbit at 60 Earth radii. Inside the tail an L1 solar-wind value does not apply.

sub_places.notes: On the way out, the IGRF model (Earth's internal field only) stops being valid past a few Earth radii: the field is shaped by the solar wind and ends at the magnetopause, about 10 Earth radii sunward of Earth (context.magnetopause_standoff). B_total_nT is not IGRF: it is the field measured now by the GOES magnetometer in geostationary orbit, about 6.6 Earth radii from Earth's centre, inside the magnetosphere. No live magnetometer sits at the magnetopause itself, and no source gives a single field value there. Beyond it the field is the interplanetary field (context.interplanetary_L1_nT, and sub-place mars_transit.cruise). NOAA notes that strong solar wind can push the magnetopause inside geostationary orbit.

magnetopause_standoff.note: NOAA: on the dayside the magnetic field is confined to within about 10 Earth radii; on the night side it is stretched out to hundreds of Earth radii. The distance moves with solar-wind pressure.

radiation_context.text: Mars surface: Curiosity's RAD instrument measured an average of 0.67 millisieverts per day at Gale crater from August 2012 to June 2013 (NASA/JPL; Hassler et al. 2014). Mars has no active global magnetic field today (Langlais et al. 2019). The measurement is from Gale crater.

sub_places.opm_note: requires magnetic shielding / field nulling coils (QuSpin operates in a shielded or compensated environment)

nv_zeeman_shift_MHz.source: SpinDrift calculation; 28.025 MHz/mT is the electron gyromagnetic ratio gamma_e/2pi (CODATA 2022, 28 024.951 3861 MHz/T, rounded to five digits; data/quantum_constants.json electron.gyromagnetic_ratio_over_2pi)
nv_zeeman_shift_MHz.note: formula: 28.025 MHz/mT x |B|; inputs: mars_surface.insight.B_total_nT; |B| in mT = nT x 1e-6; shift of one NV resonance line for a field along the NV axis (the two lines separate by twice this)

ratio_to_earth_surface.note: formula: |B| / IGRF |B| at Johnson Space Center; inputs: mars_surface.insight.B_total_nT, meta.reference.earth_surface_nT (earth_flight.jsc)

sub_places.notes: Mars has no global dynamo field today; it has a remanent crustal field that may reach several thousand nT locally (Langlais et al. 2019). B_total_nT is the mean surface field measured on the Martian surface by the InSight lander's magnetometer. For comparison, the Langlais et al. (2019) orbital model evaluated at the lander gives 312 nT.
